preS1Baseline.what: parent of S1's merge — the compiler before the fix

outcomeRule: HIT iff all 12 are charged (Calor0410) or refused and none launders silently; MISS if any shape is still silent OR any of the 7 controls regressed
discriminationPin: Gate 14 asks that reverting either half of S1 turn a DIFFERENT set of rows red. Satisfied here with a real compiler instead of a synthetic revert: the pre-S1 build at 0defc5dc reproduces #1136's frozen table EXACTLY — the same 7 charged (shape 7 with its Calor0410+Calor0411 signature) and the same 5 at exit 0 with Calor0425. That is what establishes the twelve fixtures are not vacuous: they reproduce the frozen before-state on an independently built compiler from before the fix.
disclosures: The two shapes #1136 carries as disclosures (inherited field unqualified; module-qualified module function from inside a class body) are reported by Disclosure_ShapesAreReported_NeverScored and are NOT in the denominator of 12.

nameCollision.warning: The bare name PP-S1 is AMBIGUOUS in this repository, and the ambiguity points the wrong way. docs/plans/agent-native-gates.md:340 registers PP-S1 as "converter fidelity is movable", and A-1.7 (line 1251) adjudicated THAT PP-S1 = MISS with the real-scale venue RETIRED (line 1257). So the repository's own registration record, grepped for "PP-S1", answers MISS / venue retired — the opposite of this ledger's result for a different proof point of the same name.
nameCollision.resolution: This proof point is PP-S1(rows) everywhere. The v0.12 name is frozen prose in a closed plan and is not renamed retrospectively.
nameCollision.annexScope: PP-S1(rows) is deliberately NOT registered in the A-annex: that annex governs agent-native experiments with spend and power (its PP rows are byte-frozen by scripts/check-annex-freeze.py). This proof point runs inside dotnet test with zero agent runs, and is registered in the release roadmap instead.

processFindings.finding: The instrument was vacuous as first written
processFindings.detail: The scored assertion was `!(no errors && Calor0425)`. A fixture with a typo produces a parse or bind error, HasErrors goes true, and the row passes GREEN while measuring nothing. Closed by asserting (a) no error below Calor0300 — lexer, parser and semantic codes, none of which this table is about — and (b) Calor0410 is present. The per-row expected verdicts did not change; the check got stricter, not looser.

processFindings.finding: A stale Release binary produced a false MISS
processFindings.detail: The first CLI measurement used src/Calor.Compiler/bin/Release from Sep 1 18:17. S1 landed Sep 2 19:07. That pre-S1 binary reported 5 of 12 still escaping — a MISS that would have blocked M4 for no reason. Caught by checking the artifact's timestamp against the fix's merge date. The same accident then supplied the discrimination pin, which is why it is rebuilt from 0defc5dc here rather than left as an artifact.

processFindings.finding: The first CLI invocation measured the CLI's own help text
processFindings.detail: `calor build <file>` is not a subcommand; the run printed usage, and grepping it for Calor codes matched the option descriptions, yielding an identical fake diagnostic set for all twelve rows. The real invocation is `-i <src> -o <out>`, which is what ppw-seeded-compiles.json's own `invocation` field records.
